pellegrini-s-espresso-bar.name: Pellegrini's Espresso Bar
pellegrini-s-espresso-bar.summary: A café on Bourke Street in Melbourne opened in 1954, among the city's first to use an authentic Italian espresso machine and help start its coffee culture.

h-ng.name: Hāngī
h-ng.summary: Traditional Māori method of cooking food with heated rocks in an underground pit oven, still used today for large gatherings on special occasions.

william-chen-wing-young.name: William Wing Young
william-chen-wing-young.summary: William Chen Wing Young: Chinese-Australian businessman in Melbourne (1896–1974), known for inventing and popularising the dim sim, or 'dimmy', in the 1940s.

dim-sim.name: Dim sim
dim-sim.summary: Deep-fried, thick-skinned meat dumpling popular in Australia, inspired by Cantonese dim sum and popularised in the 1940s by Chinese-Australian William Wing Young.

sweet-potato.name: Kūmara
sweet-potato.summary: A starchy, sweet-tasting root vegetable native to tropical South America, a staple food in many regions and only distantly related to the true potato.

m-ngere.name: Māngere
m-ngere.summary: A suburb of South Auckland, New Zealand, on the Manukau Harbour, historically home to Māori agricultural sites and later one of Auckland's largest state housing developments.

vittoria-coffee.name: Vittoria Coffee
vittoria-coffee.summary: Australian coffee brand made by Vittoria Food and Beverage.

dargaville.name: Dargaville
dargaville.summary: A town in New Zealand's North Island known for its large Croatian-descended population and as the country's leading kūmara (sweet potato) growing area.

northland-region.name: Northland
northland-region.summary: A region in the far north of New Zealand known for its warm weather, whose major city is Whangārei and largest town Kerikeri.

georgie-pie.name: Georgie Pie
georgie-pie.summary: A New Zealand fast-food chain specializing in meat pies, founded in 1977 as a homegrown rival to McDonald's; it was bought out in 1996 and later revived in limited form.

papunya.name: Papunya
papunya.summary: A small Indigenous Australian community northwest of Alice Springs, known as the birthplace of the 1970s dot-painting movement that shaped contemporary Indigenous Australian art.

clifford-possum-tjapaltjarri.name: Clifford Possum Tjapaltjarri
clifford-possum-tjapaltjarri.summary: Australian Aboriginal painter (1932–2002), one of the most collected Australian Indigenous artists, with works in major national galleries and the Royal Collection.

kaapa-tjampitjinpa.name: Kaapa Tjampitjinpa
kaapa-tjampitjinpa.summary: Indigenous Australian artist (c. 1920-1989) of Anmatyerre, Warlpiri and Arrernte heritage, a founding member and first chairman of the Papunya Tula artists company.

geoffrey-bardon.name: Geoffrey Bardon
geoffrey-bardon.summary: An Australian art teacher (1940-2003) who in 1971 encouraged Aboriginal children and elders at Papunya to paint traditional Dreamings, sparking the Western Desert art movement.

archibald-prize.name: Archibald Prize
archibald-prize.summary: Australia's most prestigious portrait painting prize, first awarded in 1921 from a bequest by J. F. Archibald, editor of The Bulletin.

harold-desbrowe-annear.name: Harold Desbrowe-Annear
harold-desbrowe-annear.summary: Influential Australian architect (1865–1933) at the forefront of the Arts and Crafts movement, who founded Melbourne's T-Square club in 1900.

sir-john-sulman-prize.name: Sir John Sulman Prize
sir-john-sulman-prize.summary: One of Australia's longest-running art prizes, established in 1936 and held alongside the Archibald and Wynne prizes at the Art Gallery of New South Wales.

henry-hanke.name: Henry Hanke
henry-hanke.summary: Australian painter and teacher (1901 to 1989) who won the Archibald Prize in 1934 with a self-portrait and the first Sulman Prize in 1936.

tiwi-islands.name: Tiwi Islands
tiwi-islands.summary: A group of islands off Australia's Northern Territory, home to the Aboriginal Tiwi people, whose society today blends traditional beliefs with Catholicism brought by European settlers.

brewarrina-aboriginal-fish-traps.name: Brewarrina Aboriginal Cultural Museum
brewarrina-aboriginal-fish-traps.summary: Museum opened in 1988 beside the ancient Aboriginal fish traps at Brewarrina, New South Wales, Australia.

barwon-river-new-south-wales.name: Barwon River
barwon-river-new-south-wales.summary: A river in north-western New South Wales, Australia, part of the Murray–Darling basin; its Aboriginal name means 'great, wide, awful river of muddy water.'

humpy.name: Gunyah
humpy.summary: A small, temporary Australian Aboriginal shelter made of branches and bark, often built against a tree for support; also called a humpy, wurley or mia-mia.

art-australia.name: Art + Australia
art-australia.summary: Australia's longest-running art journal, a biannual magazine that succeeded Art in Australia in 1963 and became digital-only in 2022.

art-in-australia.name: Art in Australia
art-in-australia.summary: An Australian art magazine published between 1916 and 1942.

mervyn-horton.name: Mervyn Horton
mervyn-horton.summary: An Australian art editor, art collector and philanthropist (1917-1983).

biennale-of-sydney.name: Biennale of Sydney
biennale-of-sydney.summary: An international contemporary art festival held every two years in Sydney, one of the longest-running exhibitions of its kind and the first biennale established in the Asia-Pacific region.

sydney-festival.name: Sydney Festival
sydney-festival.summary: An annual three-week arts festival held in Sydney, Australia, running since 1977 and featuring music, dance, theatre and visual arts.

shirley-purdie.name: Shirley Purdie
shirley-purdie.summary: Contemporary Indigenous Australian artist (born 1947) from the Warmun Community in Western Australia, who won the 2007 Blake Prize for Religious Art.

blake-prize.name: Blake Prize
blake-prize.summary: An Australian art prize for works exploring spirituality, first awarded in 1951 (initially named the Blake Prize for Religious Art) and given annually until 2015.

gloria-petyarre.name: Gloria Petyarre
gloria-petyarre.summary: Aboriginal Australian artist (1942-2021) from the Anmatyerre community, best known for her 'Bush Medicine' paintings.

wynne-prize.name: Wynne Prize
wynne-prize.summary: One of Australia's longest-running art prizes, established in 1897 for the best landscape painting or figure sculpture of Australian scenery, awarded alongside the Archibald Prize.

claude-monet.name: Claude Monet
claude-monet.summary: French painter (1840–1926) and founder of Impressionism, known for outdoor landscape paintings capturing his perceptions of light and nature.

henri-matisse.name: Henri Matisse
henri-matisse.summary: French painter (1869 to 1954), known for bold use of colour; alongside Picasso, he helped define modern art's revolutionary developments in the early 20th century.

tarnanthi.name: Tarnanthi
tarnanthi.summary: An annual festival of contemporary Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander art held in Adelaide, South Australia.

rhana-devenport.name: Rhana Devenport
rhana-devenport.summary: An Australian-born art curator who directed the Auckland Art Gallery from 2013 to 2018 before becoming director of the Art Gallery of South Australia.

australian-and-new-zealand-army-corps.name: ANZAC
australian-and-new-zealand-army-corps.summary: A First World War army corps of the British Empire, formed in Egypt in December 1914 from mostly Australian and New Zealand troops, that fought at Gallipoli under General William Birdwood.
australian-and-new-zealand-army-corps.source_title: Australian and New Zealand Army Corps

gallipoli.name: Gallipoli
gallipoli.summary: A peninsula in European Turkey between the Aegean Sea and the Dardanelles, its Italianized name meaning 'beautiful city,' anciently known as the Thracian Chersonese.

first-fleet.name: First Fleet
first-fleet.summary: Eleven British ships that carried over 1,400 convicts, marines and settlers to Australia in 1787–1788, founding the first British colony at Port Jackson.

german-new-guinea.name: German New Guinea
german-new-guinea.summary: A German colonial territory covering the northeastern part of New Guinea and nearby Pacific islands, held from 1884 until it fell to Australian and Japanese forces in World War I.

australian-naval-and-military-expedition.name: Australian Naval and Military Expeditionary Force
australian-naval-and-military-expedition.summary: A roughly 2,000-strong Australian volunteer force raised in 1914 to seize and destroy German wireless stations in German New Guinea, then occupying the territory for the rest of World War I.
australian-naval-and-military-expedition.source_title: Australian Naval and Military Expeditionary Force

ahs-centaur.name: AHS Centaur
ahs-centaur.summary: An Australian hospital ship torpedoed by a Japanese submarine off Queensland on 14 May 1943, killing 268 of the 332 people aboard.

first-australian-imperial-force.name: AIF (First Australian Imperial Force)
first-australian-imperial-force.summary: Main Australian expeditionary force of the First World War, formed in 1914, which fought at Gallipoli and on the Western Front and gained a reputation as a highly effective volunteer force.

coniston-massacre.name: Coniston massacre
coniston-massacre.summary: A series of killings of Indigenous Australians near Coniston cattle station in 1928, the last officially sanctioned massacre of Aboriginal people, with estimated deaths in the dozens to hundreds.

german-submarine-u-862.name: U-862
german-submarine-u-862.summary: A Type IXD2 German U-boat of World War II that sank seven ships and, after Germany's surrender, was taken over by Japan and renamed I-502.

batavia-dutch-east-indies.name: Batavia
batavia-dutch-east-indies.summary: A Dutch colonial port city founded in 1619 on the site of Jayakarta, on the location of modern Jakarta, which served for about 320 years as capital of the Dutch East Indies.

david-unaipon.name: David Unaipon
david-unaipon.summary: An Aboriginal Australian author, inventor and preacher (1872–1967) who wrote essays and stories drawn from oral traditions, held ten patents, and by the late 1920s was one of Australia's best-known Aboriginal people.

oodgeroo-noonuccal.name: Oodgeroo Noonuccal
oodgeroo-noonuccal.summary: Aboriginal Australian poet, artist and rights activist (1920–1993), formerly known as Kath Walker, who in 1964 became the first Aboriginal Australian to publish a book of poetry.

sally-morgan-artist.name: Sally Morgan
sally-morgan-artist.summary: An Australian Aboriginal author, dramatist and artist born in 1951, whose works are held in private and public collections around the world.

peter-carey-novelist.name: Peter Carey
peter-carey-novelist.summary: Australian novelist who has won the Booker Prize twice, for Oscar and Lucinda (1988) and True History of the Kelly Gang (2001).

miles-franklin-award.name: Miles Franklin Award
miles-franklin-award.summary: Australia's leading annual literary prize for a novel of high merit depicting Australian life, funded by the estate of writer Miles Franklin (1879–1954) and worth A$60,000 as of 2025.

oscar-and-lucinda.name: Oscar and Lucinda
oscar-and-lucinda.summary: A novel by Australian author Peter Carey that won the 1988 Booker Prize and the 1989 Miles Franklin Award.

true-history-of-the-kelly-gang.name: True History of the Kelly Gang
true-history-of-the-kelly-gang.summary: A 2000 novel by Peter Carey, written as a fictional memoir loosely based on the life of Australian bushranger Ned Kelly, which won the 2001 Booker Prize.
true-history-of-the-kelly-gang.source_title: True History of the Kelly Gang

kim-scott.name: Kim Scott
kim-scott.summary: Australian novelist, born in 1957, of Aboriginal Australian ancestry and a descendant of the Noongar people of Western Australia.

thea-astley.name: Thea Astley
thea-astley.summary: Australian novelist and short story writer (1925–2004) who won more Miles Franklin Awards, Australia's top literary prize, than any other writer, publishing steadily from 1958.

alexis-wright.name: Alexis Wright
alexis-wright.summary: Australian writer born in 1950, the first person to win the Stella Prize twice and the first to win both the Stella Prize and Miles Franklin Award in the same year.

benang-from-the-heart.name: Benang: From the Heart
benang-from-the-heart.summary: A 1999 novel by Indigenous Australian author Kim Scott that shared the 2000 Miles Franklin Award with Thea Astley's Drylands.

carpentaria-novel.name: Carpentaria
carpentaria-novel.summary: A 2006 novel by Indigenous Australian author Alexis Wright that won Australia's leading literary prize, the Miles Franklin Award, in 2007.

magabala-books.name: Magabala Books
magabala-books.summary: Indigenous Australian publishing house founded in 1987 in Broome, Western Australia, dedicated to preserving Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultures.

jack-davis-playwright.name: Jack Davis
jack-davis-playwright.summary: Australian Aboriginal playwright, poet, and activist (1917–2000) who did not focus on writing until his fifties, later gaining international recognition for his plays.

jagardoo-poems-from-aboriginal-australia.name: Jagardoo
jagardoo-poems-from-aboriginal-australia.summary: 1978 poetry collection, the second by Noongar playwright and poet Jack Davis, often called the 20th century's Aboriginal Poet Laureate.

noongar.name: Noongar
noongar.summary: Aboriginal Australian people of south-west Western Australia, made up of 14 related groups sharing largely mutually intelligible languages and dialects.

gerald-glaskin.name: Gerald Glaskin
gerald-glaskin.summary: Australian author (1923-2000), known by the byline G. M. Glaskin.

dorothy-porter.name: Dorothy Porter
dorothy-porter.summary: Australian poet (1954–2008) who received the Christopher Brennan Award for lifetime achievement in poetry.

kenneth-mackenzie-author.name: Seaforth Mackenzie
kenneth-mackenzie-author.summary: Australian poet and novelist (1913–1955) who wrote under the pen name Seaforth Mackenzie, best known for his 1937 novel The Young Desire It.

the-young-desire-it.name: The Young Desire It
the-young-desire-it.summary: A 1937 novel by Australian author Seaforth Mackenzie that won the ALS Gold Medal for Best Novel that year.

als-gold-medal.name: Australian Literature Society Gold Medal
als-gold-medal.summary: An annual Australian literary prize, awarded from 1928 by the Australian Literature Society and later by the Association for the Study of Australian Literature.

science-technology-australia.name: Science & Technology Australia
science-technology-australia.summary: Australia's peak body for science and technology, representing over 90,000 scientists and technologists; known as the Federation of Australian Scientific and Technological Societies until 2011.

barry-jones-australian-politician.name: Barry Jones
barry-jones-australian-politician.summary: An Australian writer, teacher, lawyer, social activist, quiz champion and former Labor Party politician who campaigned against the death penalty in the 1960s, notably opposing Ronald Ryan's execution.

academy-of-the-social-sciences-in-austra.name: Academy of the Social Sciences in Australia
academy-of-the-social-sciences-in-austra.summary: An independent Australian organisation founded in 1971 to advance social science research, with over 750 elected fellows advising government on national issues.
academy-of-the-social-sciences-in-austra.source_title: Academy of the Social Sciences in Australia

superstars-of-stem.name: Superstars of STEM
superstars-of-stem.summary: A program run by Science & Technology Australia since 2017 that trains women and non-binary people in STEM to become public role models and media voices.

harold-holt.name: Harold Holt
harold-holt.summary: 17th prime minister of Australia (1966–1967), whose term ended with his disappearance and presumed death while swimming at a surf beach.

john-gorton.name: John Gorton
john-gorton.summary: 19th Prime Minister of Australia (1968–1971), Liberal Party leader and the only prime minister to have come from the upper house of Parliament; earlier a WWII fighter pilot.

science-party-australia.name: The Science Party
science-party-australia.summary: Australian political party founded in 2013 as the Future Party, renamed in 2016, that ran candidates in three federal elections before deregistration in 2022 and merger into the Fusion Party.

kirby-institute.name: Kirby Institute
kirby-institute.summary: A medical research organisation affiliated with the University of New South Wales, founded in 1986, originally focused on HIV/AIDS and later expanded to other infectious diseases.

statute-of-westminster-1931.name: Statute of Westminster 1931
statute-of-westminster-1931.summary: A 1931 UK law that greatly increased the self-governing Dominions' independence from Britain, removing most of Parliament's power to legislate for them.

william-mcmahon.name: William McMahon
william-mcmahon.summary: 20th prime minister of Australia (1971–1972) and Liberal Party leader who previously held several ministerial posts, including Treasurer, before losing office to Gough Whitlam's Labor Party.

gough-whitlam.name: Gough Whitlam
gough-whitlam.summary: Australia's 21st prime minister (1972–1975), whose reformist Labor government ended with his controversial dismissal by the governor-general during the 1975 constitutional crisis.

protector-of-aborigines.name: Chief Protector of Aborigines
protector-of-aborigines.summary: An Australian colonial office overseeing Indigenous affairs from the 1830s; from the 1890s it often controlled where Aboriginal people lived and whom they could marry.

aboriginal-protection-board.name: Aborigines Protection Board
aboriginal-protection-board.summary: Name for various historical Australian state-run bodies that controlled Aboriginal Australians' lives, including where they could live and work, and played a key role in the Stolen Generations.

charles-duguid.name: Charles Duguid
charles-duguid.summary: Scottish-born Australian doctor, social reformer and Aboriginal rights campaigner (1884–1986) who founded the Ernabella mission station and was given the honorific 'Tjilpi' by the Pitjantjatjara people.

neville-bonner.name: Neville Bonner
neville-bonner.summary: Australian politician (1922-1999) who became the first Aboriginal Australian in Parliament in 1971, and in 1972 the first Indigenous Australian elected by popular vote.

aden-ridgeway.name: Aden Ridgeway
aden-ridgeway.summary: Australian former politician (born 1962) who served in the Senate for New South Wales from 1999 to 2005, the only Indigenous member of parliament during his term.

nova-peris.name: Nova Peris
nova-peris.summary: An Aboriginal Australian athlete who became the first Aboriginal Australian to win Olympic gold, in field hockey in 1996, and later served as an Australian senator from 2013 to 2016.

jacqui-lambie.name: Jacqui Lambie
jacqui-lambie.summary: Australian politician and former soldier, senator for Tasmania since 2019, who founded the Jacqui Lambie Network after leaving the Palmer United Party in 2014.

pat-dodson.name: Pat Dodson
pat-dodson.summary: An Australian Indigenous rights activist, born 1948, nicknamed the 'father of reconciliation'; he served as a Labor senator for Western Australia from 2016 to 2024.

stolen-generations.name: Stolen Generations
stolen-generations.summary: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children forcibly removed from their families by Australian government agencies and churches, roughly 1905 to 1967; a 1997 report called it genocide.

fusion-party-australia.name: Fusion Party (Australia)
fusion-party-australia.summary: An Australian political party formed by merging the Science, Pirate, Secular, Vote Planet and Climate Change Justice parties, which in 2025 allied with the Australian Progressives and Democracy First.

raukkan-south-australia.name: Point McLeay Mission
raukkan-south-australia.summary: A Christian mission established in 1859 for the Ngarrindjeri people, later made an Aboriginal reserve in 1916 and handed back to the Ngarrindjeri in 1974, renamed Raukkan in 1982.

point-pearce-south-australia.name: Point Pearce
point-pearce-south-australia.summary: A town in South Australia established in 1868 as a mission for Aboriginal people, later becoming a government-run Aboriginal reserve.

killalpaninna-mission.name: Killalpaninna Mission
killalpaninna-mission.summary: A Lutheran mission for Aboriginal people in northeast South Australia, founded by German missionaries and active from 1866 to 1915.

koonibba.name: Koonibba
koonibba.summary: Aboriginal community locality in South Australia that grew around the Koonibba Mission (1901–1975); home to the oldest still-existing Aboriginal football club, founded in 1906.

2017-18-australian-parliamentary-eligibi.name: Australian Citizenship Crisis
2017-18-australian-parliamentary-eligibi.summary: Constitutional crisis beginning in 2017 in which fifteen members of Australia's Parliament, ruled ineligible over dual citizenship, were disqualified by the High Court or resigned.

division-of-grayndler.name: Division of Grayndler
division-of-grayndler.summary: Australian federal electoral division covering Sydney's Inner West, represented since 1996 by Anthony Albanese, Prime Minister of Australia since 2022.

john-anderson-philosopher.name: John Anderson
john-anderson-philosopher.summary: Scottish philosopher (1893–1962) who was Challis Professor of Philosophy at Sydney University from 1927 to 1958 and founded Australian realism.

j-l-mackie.name: J. L. Mackie
j-l-mackie.summary: Australian philosopher (1917–1981) known for work in ethics and philosophy of religion, including his defence of moral scepticism and atheism in Ethics: Inventing Right and Wrong.

david-malet-armstrong.name: David Malet Armstrong
david-malet-armstrong.summary: An Australian philosopher (1926–2014) known for his work on metaphysics and philosophy of mind, credited with helping shape the field's agenda and debates.

sydney-push.name: Sydney Push
sydney-push.summary: A left-wing libertarian intellectual subculture centred on pub life in Sydney from the late 1940s to the early 1970s, including students, writers and academics.

j-j-c-smart.name: J. J. C. Smart
j-j-c-smart.summary: A British-Australian philosopher (1920–2012) who worked in metaphysics, philosophy of science, philosophy of mind, philosophy of religion and political philosophy, and wrote for the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.

ullin-place.name: Ullin Place
ullin-place.summary: A British philosopher and psychologist (1924–2000) whose 1956 paper 'Is Consciousness a Brain Process?' launched the identity theory of mind.

gilbert-ryle.name: Gilbert Ryle
gilbert-ryle.summary: British philosopher (1900 to 1976) known for critiquing Cartesian dualism and coining the phrase 'ghost in the machine' in his book The Concept of Mind.

type-physicalism.name: Mind–brain identity theory (type physicalism)
type-physicalism.summary: Philosophy of mind theory holding that types of mental events, such as pain, correspond directly to types of physical events in the brain.

graham-oppy.name: Graham Oppy
graham-oppy.summary: Australian philosopher born in 1960, specializing in philosophy of religion, and professor at Monash University in Melbourne.

samuel-alexander.name: Samuel Alexander
samuel-alexander.summary: An Australian-born British philosopher (1859–1938), best known for developing the theory of emergentism in biology.

graham-nerlich.name: Graham Nerlich
graham-nerlich.summary: An Australian philosopher (1929–2022) and Emeritus Professor at the University of Adelaide, known for arguing that space is a real entity rather than merely relational.

max-charlesworth.name: Max Charlesworth
max-charlesworth.summary: Australian philosopher (1925–2014) who wrote on religion, Aboriginal culture, bioethics and education, honored in 1990 for his contributions to Australian society.

sophia-journal.name: Sophia (journal)
sophia-journal.summary: A quarterly academic journal on philosophy, metaphysics, religion and ethics, founded in 1962 by Max Charlesworth and Graeme de Graaf.

james-franklin-philosopher.name: James Franklin
james-franklin-philosopher.summary: An Australian philosopher, mathematician and historian of ideas, born in 1953.

leichhardt-new-south-wales.name: Leichhardt
leichhardt-new-south-wales.summary: A suburb in the Inner West of Sydney, Australia, about 5 kilometers from the city center, known for a high concentration of Italian immigrants.

cathy-freeman.name: Cathy Freeman
cathy-freeman.summary: Australian sprinter and the first female Indigenous Australian Commonwealth Games gold medalist, who won the 400 metres at the 2000 Sydney Olympics after lighting the Olympic Flame.

arthur-beetson.name: Arthur Beetson
arthur-beetson.summary: An Australian rugby league player and coach (1945–2011) who became the first Indigenous Australian to captain his country in any sport.

mark-ella.name: Mark Ella
mark-ella.summary: Indigenous Australian rugby union player (born 1959) capped 25 times for the Wallabies; captain of Australia from 1982 to 1983, he later starred in the 1984 Grand Slam tour of Britain and Ireland, scoring a try in each Test.

australia-national-rugby-league-team.name: Kangaroos
australia-national-rugby-league-team.summary: Australia's national rugby league team, nicknamed the Kangaroos since 1908, the most successful side in Rugby League World Cup history with 12 titles.
